title: Japanese City Accused of Adding 2,000 Fake Residents
paragraphs: Japan has a big problem — its population is getting smaller every year. In fact, the country had about 3 million fewer people in 2025 than it did just five years earlier. Last year, the number of people fell in every part of the country except Tokyo.
But while the population of many cities is falling, one city in central Japan appears to have gained thousands of new residents.
There's just one problem — these people don't exist!

Officials in the city of Toyama are accused of adding more than 2,000 extra people to its population records. The city said its population was just over 402,000, but the real number was later found to be under 400,000.
Every five years, Japan takes a census to count how many people live in the country. This helps the country's central government decide how much money to give local governments.
And police believe that city workers changed some records to make it look like people were living in empty homes in Toyama.
This may have brought the city extra money. Toyama could have received 60 million yen, or around $380,000, more than it should have.

Police have searched the city's government offices as part of the investigation. If city officials are found guilty of changing the numbers, they could have to pay a fine, or spend up to six months in prison.
